summaryBox.title: Nernst Equation
summaryBox.takeaway: E_cell = E°_cell - (0.05916 / n) log₁₀ Q at 298 K. As Q increases (more products), cell potential E_cell decreases.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NERNST EQUATION AT 298 K

E_cell = E°_cell - (0.05916 / n) log₁₀ Q

where n is moles of electrons transferred, and Q = [Products]^c / [Reactants]^a
conceptBreakdown.content:
For a general redox reaction $aA + bB \rightleftharpoons cC + dD$:
$$E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{RT}{nF} \ln Q = \mathbf{E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.05916}{n} \log_{10} Q \quad (\text{at } 298.15\text{ K})}$$
• Pure solids and pure liquids have unit activity (1.0) and are excluded from $Q$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Thermodynamic Coupling & Equilibrium Constant (K_eq)
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Thermodynamic Coupling & Equilibrium Constant (K_eq)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THERMODYNAMICS & EQUILIBRIUM COUPLING

1. Gibbs Free Energy: Δ_r G = -n F E_cell  |  Δ_r G° = -n F E°_cell
   (Spontaneous if E_cell > 0 ⟹ Δ_r G < 0)

2. Equilibrium Constant (K_eq):
   At equilibrium, E_cell = 0 and Q = K_eq ⟹ log₁₀ K_eq = (n × E°_cell) / 0.05916
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Free Energy**: $\mathbf{\Delta_r G = -n F E_{\text{cell}}}$. A positive cell potential corresponds to a thermodynamically spontaneous reaction.
• **Equilibrium Constant**: When the cell is completely discharged ($E_{\text{cell}} = 0$), $Q = K_{\text{eq}}$:
$$\mathbf{\log_{10} K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{n E^\circ_{\text{cell}}}{0.05916} \implies K_{\text{eq}} = 10^{\frac{n E^\circ_{\text{cell}}}{0.05916}}}$$
